title: Impact of Paid Family Leave on Women's Labor Force Participation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

This is a classic DID setup: we have treated states (those implementing paid family leave laws) and control states, observed before and after policy implementation. The `treat_x_post` interaction term is the DID estimator.

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of the paid family leave law, treated and control states would have followed the same trend in women's log labor force participation. This is plausible if states that adopted the law were not already on divergent trajectories relative to control states.

Additional assumptions include: (1) no spillover effects between treated and control states (SUTVA), (2) no contemporaneous shocks differentially affecting treated states, and (3) treatment timing is uniform across treated states.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# DID Analysis: Paid Family Leave on Women's LFP
# ============================================================

library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(fixest)

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s42_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "x", ncol(df), "\n")
cat("\nSummary:\n")
summary(df)

# Check design balance
cat("\n=== Design Summary ===\n")
cat("Unique units:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", length(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated units:", length(unique(df$unit_id[df$treated == 1])), "\n")
cat("Control units:", length(unique(df$unit_id[df$treated == 0])), "\n")
table(df$treated, df$post, dnn = c("Treated", "Post"))

# ============================================================
# 1. BASELINE DID: Simple OLS with interaction
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 1: Baseline DID (OLS) ===\n")
did_base <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(did_base)

cat("\nDID Estimate (treat_x_post):", coef(did_base)["treat_x_post"], "\n")

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== Model 1 with Robust SEs ===\n")
robust_test <- coeftest(did_base, vcov = vcovHC(did_base, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_test)

# ============================================================
# 2. DID with Unit and Time Fixed Effects
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 2: Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) ===\n")
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(did_twfe)

# Cluster standard errors at the unit (state) level
cat("\n=== Model 2 with Clustered SEs (by unit) ===\n")
did_twfe_cl <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                     data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(did_twfe_cl)

# ============================================================
# 3. Manual DID Calculation (2x2 means)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Manual DID Calculation ===\n")
means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(means)

y_t1 <- means$y[means$treated == 1 & means$post == 1]
y_t0 <- means$y[means$treated == 1 & means$post == 0]
y_c1 <- means$y[means$treated == 0 & means$post == 1]
y_c0 <- means$y[means$treated == 0 & means$post == 0]

did_manual <- (y_t1 - y_t0) - (y_c1 - y_c0)
cat("\nMean(Treated, Post):", y_t1, "\n")
cat("Mean(Treated, Pre):", y_t0, "\n")
cat("Mean(Control, Post):", y_c1, "\n")
cat("Mean(Control, Pre):", y_c0, "\n")
cat("Manual DID estimate:", did_manual, "\n")

# ============================================================
# 4. Robustness: Parallel Trends Check (if multiple pre-periods)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Event Study / Period-Specific Effects ===\n")
n_periods <- length(unique(df$period))
if (n_periods > 2) {
  df$period_f <- factor(df$period)
  # Event study with period interactions
  es_model <- feols(y ~ i(period, treated, ref = max(df$period[df$post == 0])) | 
                      unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
  summary(es_model)
  cat("\nEvent study coefficients (pre-treatment should be ~0 for parallel trends):\n")
} else {
  cat("Only 2 periods detected — cannot run event study.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# 5. Robustness: Placebo test (treat effect in pre-period only)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Pre-Treatment Difference ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
pre_test <- lm(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
cat("Pre-treatment difference between treated and control:\n")
print(coeftest(pre_test, vcov = vcovHC(pre_test, type = "HC1")))

# ============================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("FINAL RESULTS SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Baseline DID coefficient:", round(coef(did_base)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Baseline p-value:", round(summary(did_base)$coefficients["treat_x_post", 4], 4), "\n")
cat("TWFE DID coefficient:", round(coef(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Manual DID:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")
cat("========================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive.** Paid family leave laws are hypothesized to increase women's labor force participation by reducing the career penalty of childbearing — women can take leave and return to their jobs rather than exiting the labor force entirely.

**Expected magnitude:** The DID coefficient on `treat_x_post` should be positive, likely in the range of **0.05–0.30 log points** (roughly 5–30% increase), depending on the simulation's data-generating process. The empirical literature (e.g., Rossin-Slater et al. 2013; Baum & Ruhm 2016) finds modest but significant positive effects, typically 2–10 percentage points.

**Robustness expectations:**
- Pre-treatment coefficients in the event study should be statistically insignificant (supporting parallel trends).
- The pre-treatment difference test should show no significant gap between treated and control, confirming the DID design validity.
- Results should be robust to clustering at the state level and inclusion of unit/time fixed effects.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare changes in women's labor force participation in states with and without the law over time.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The implementation of paid family leave laws is associated with an increase in women's labor force participation.
